audit_findings.title: Growth may be valued without the land and inventory reinvestment it requires
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 inventory increase $179.457m (44.0% of $407.4m anchor OE); H1 2026 inventory increase $73.554m; normalized valuation adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Projected OE and growth omit incremental inventory and working-capital funding, overstating cash distributable to equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Because these costs are capitalized as a component of our inventories and are not recognized in our statement of operations until a home is delivered, we incur significant cash outflows prior to recognizing earnings from a delivered home.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated by the stated method, while the normalized deduction remains unresolved. The filed cash requirements are large relative to anchor OE and are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a cycle-wide reconciliation of inventory, deposits, receivables and operating liabilities required for growth; deduct normalized incremental reinvestment in each scenario and rerun all values.

audit_findings.title: The stated interest-retention rail is weakened by capitalized interest
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 incurred interest exceeded amortized interest by $3.240m; H1 2026 excess was $19.577m; capitalized-interest balance was $145.204m at May 31, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest is deferred into inventory and enters OE through cost of sales when homes are delivered, creating timing differences between economic interest incurred and interest recognized.
audit_findings.evidence: All interest incurred in 2025 and 2024 was capitalized, as the average amount of inventory qualifying for interest capitalization exceeded the average debt level for each period.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but its normalized cycle-wide effect is unresolved. The FY2025 difference was only 0.8% of anchor OE, whereas the H1 2026 deferral reached 4.8% of anchor OE; the record cannot establish whether that larger mismatch persists or reverses.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile interest incurred, capitalized and amortized for every OE year, normalize the cycle-wide timing difference, and rerun OE without deducting ordinary debt principal if normalized economic interest remains fully captured.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains a tax benefit scheduled to disappear
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.1m, equal to 3.2% of $407.4m anchor OE; proportional base operating-PV effect approximately $184.1m or $2.87 per share, reducing base value to approximately $89.34 and buy-below to approximately $62.54
audit_findings.mechanism: The expiring Section 45L benefit inflates anchor OE and therefore projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, beginning in our 2026 third quarter, our income tax expense and effective tax rate will no longer reflect a benefit from such tax credits as to homes delivered after the effective date.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization error, not merely a possibility. On the supplied numbers, however, a proportional removal leaves the approximately $62.54 buy-below level above the $52.25 market price, so it does not change the current valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $13.1m FY2025 credit from normalized anchor OE, use the post-expiration tax rate in forecasts, and rerun the scenario table.

audit_findings.title: Positive growth scenarios may skip the disclosed near-term margin reset
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 net income $60.773m versus $217.440m, down $156.667m or 72%; housing gross margin 15.3% versus 19.7%; FY2026 guidance is $4.90bn-$5.30bn housing revenue and 16.1%-16.5% gross margin versus FY2025 $6.211bn and 19.1% adjusted margin
audit_findings.mechanism: Immediate growth from FY2025 OE bypasses the demonstrated decline in revenue, margin and earnings during the first forecast years.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our housing gross profit margin to be in the range of 15.4% to 16.0%, assuming no inventory-related charges, compared to 20.3% for the corresponding 2025 quarter.
audit_findings.explanation: The near-term reset is now demonstrated by two reported quarters, not just management guidance. Its scale is large relative to anchor OE and can materially reduce the present value of early cash flows and the earnings base from which later growth is projected.
audit_findings.action: Construct FY2026 and FY2027 OE from reported results, backlog, delivery guidance, margins and operating expenses, then apply long-run scenario growth only after the explicit near-term bridge and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity value may not all be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum exposed bridge amount $200.760m, or $3.12 per share; removing all of it would reduce buy-below by approximately $2.19 to $62.36, still $10.11 above the $52.25 price
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating liquidity is added as a separable equity asset even though it may be required to fund inventory, seasonality and covenants.
audit_findings.evidence: Our business needs considerable cash to, among other things, acquire and develop land, build homes and provide customer service.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether any cash is genuinely surplus remains unresolved, especially because KBH had $275.0m of revolver borrowings and negative $93.470m H1 2026 operating cash flow. Nevertheless, even treating the entire cash balance as non-excess would not change the supplied buy/no-buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum unrestricted operating cash through a downturn using seasonal working-capital needs, covenant liquidity and inventory funding; add only the demonstrated surplus in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Net unfunded postretirement obligations are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.6m plan liabilities less $47.0m attributable plan cash-surrender value equals a computed $14.6m deficit, or $0.23 per share and 0.25% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A net past-service obligation ahead of common equity is omitted from the equity bridge unless its settlement cash flows are already fully captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The liabilities related to these plans were $61.6 million at November 30, 2025 and $60.8 million at November 30, 2024, and are included in accrued expenses and other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross liability and dedicated insurance values are filed, producing a small computed deficit. Even deducting the full $61.6m gross liability would equal only $0.96 per share and about 1.0% of base equity value, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the $47.0m plan-specific insurance value is available for these obligations and whether projected OE captures all benefit payments; deduct any remaining unfunded amount once, avoiding double counting.
